data.name: Safiyya
data.gender_notes: Safiyya is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'safa', which means 'purity' or 'chastity'. In the Bible, there is a similar name, Sophia, which means 'wisdom'. The name Safiyya carries the meaning “Pure, Chaste” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Hebrew. Parents who choose Safiyya usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, chaste and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Reflects a pure and chaste spirit, striving for wisdom and enlightenment.
data.etymology: Safiyya belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, Chaste.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Safiyya total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Safiyya is of Arabic origin and has been a popular name in the Islamic world throughout history. It is associated with female beauty, grace, and purity. In many Muslim cultures, it is an honor to bear the name Safiyya as it signifies the high moral values and virtues held dear in Islam.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Safiyya is a reminder of the spiritual significance of purity and chastity in Islam. Being pure in thought, word, and deed is a fundamental aspect of the Islamic faith. The name also symbolizes the importance of seeking wisdom and knowledge, as Sophia does in the Bible, in one's life. By embodying these qualities, individuals can strive towards living a virtuous life and drawing closer to Allah.

historical_references.reference: Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab was a prominent woman in the early Islamic community. She was the wife of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the mother of his son, Ibrahim.
historical_references.context: Safiyya was a Jewish woman who converted to Islam after the Battle of Khaybar. She was taken as a war booty and later married to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Safiyya remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
